Conversion notes

This proof of concept converts the October 7, 2026 issue into 66 separate HTML pages. It includes news, letters, school and sports coverage, arts, features, an obituary, calendars, and newspaper notices. The branded real estate report is identified separately as a commercial feature.

What was done

PDFKit extracted the existing text and its coordinates from all 28 pages. An issue-specific map was manually assembled and checked to identify article boundaries, reading order, bylines, and continuation pages. A script reconstructs paragraphs, joins broken words, formats schedules as HTML tables, and generates the article pages. Sixteen photo and illustration crops are rendered from the original PDF.

What still needs editorial review

This is a draft conversion, not a fully automatic production pipeline. Paragraph breaks, compound-word hyphens, captions, source typos, and table transcription should be checked against the original. The PDF’s overlapping text required manual cleanup of one newspaper notice and recovery of the ReQuip byline. The library-events display title is supplied from the printed library identification. Photographs are included for selected stories; other photos remain available in the original PDF.

Coverage of the printed issue

Continuation pages are joined into the original story rather than published as duplicate articles. Article counts below include stories continued on that page. Advertisements, classifieds, staff masthead, subscription forms, display promotions, and cartoons remain in the original issue.

Reproducible source

The project retains the PDF text/layout, the article map, and a line-level provenance report in work/article-extraction/. Run python3 scripts/build-articles.py to regenerate the HTML. These mappings apply to this one issue; a new issue requires new segmentation and review.

Publishing and access

These are plain static HTML pages. If the issue is member-only, apply membership protection to this entire article folder as well as its source PDFs and page previews.
